title: KV cache - reuse, eviction, paging & memory-bandwidth investigation
content:
TL;DR:
We profiled KV cache behaviour under realistic chat and completion workloads. Key findings: reuse rates drop sharply with interleaved conversations and high concurrency due to KV fragmentation; eviction thrashing occurs when effective KV working set slightly exceeds reserved GPU KV memory; paging (host->GPU transfers) introduces variable stalls (20-150ms) that dominate tail latency when eviction/paging is frequent; measured sustained memory bandwidth during heavy paging peaks at ~180 GB/s on A100 but effective useful bandwidth is lower because of small, random transfers and CPU->GPU serialization.

Purpose:
- Understand the relationship between KV reuse, eviction policies, paging behaviour and observed latency/cost.
- Prioritize mitigations (policy changes, compaction, prefetching) that reduce tail latency and token-cost.

Test matrix / workloads:
1) Chat-sim: 8k simulated concurrent conversations, avg. turn length 120 tokens, seq_len=2048, request inter-arrival Poisson, 60/40 read/write (reads = KV reuse).
2) Completion-sim: heavy single-stream long generations, bursty arrivals (50 qps), seq_len distribution sampled from production traces.
3) Microbench: synthetic patterns controlling duplicate prefixes (reuse high) vs random prompts (reuse low).

Configurations tested:
- KV cache sizes: 8GB, 12GB, 16GB reserved (on GPU).
- Eviction policies: LRU (current), Segmented LRU (hot/cold), Time-decay LRU (age-based), Approx-LFU.
- Paging mode: synchronous page-in (blocking) vs async prefetching (work-in-progress).
- Compression: no-compression vs 2:1 lightweight compression of KV items (simulated).

Metrics collected (per-run): reuse_rate (percent of requests with KV hit), eviction_rate (items/sec), paging_events (page-ins/sec), avg_paging_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, memory_bandwidth_GBps (measured by nvprof/metrics), throughput_rps, cost_token_estimate.

Representative results (chat-sim, 12GB KV):
- Baseline (LRU, sync paging): reuse_rate=37%, eviction_rate=420 items/s, paging_events=310/s, avg_paging_latency_ms=48ms, p95_latency=320ms, p99_latency=580ms, mem_bw_peak=178GB/s.
- Segmented LRU (2 segments): reuse_rate=42% (+5pt), eviction_rate=280 items/s (-33%), paging_events=190/s, avg_paging_latency=31ms, p95_latency=260ms, p99_latency=420ms.
- Time-decay LRU (age timeout 5m): reuse_rate=39%, eviction_rate=240 items/s, paging_events=170/s, avg_paging_latency=28ms, p95_latency=245ms, p99_latency=400ms.
- Compression (2:1) + SegLRU: effective KV working set fits in 12GB -> reuse_rate=47%, eviction_rate=110 items/s, paging_events=60/s, avg_paging_latency=14ms, p95_latency=190ms, p99_latency=280ms.

Observations / interpretation:
- Reuse rate sensitivity: reuse correlates strongly with prefix overlap and user concurrency patterns. Small increases in reuse (5-10pt) yield outsized tail latency reductions because they avoid expensive page-ins and eviction churn.
- Eviction thrash: when working set is near capacity, simple LRU causes hot items to be evicted then reloaded (thrashing). Segmented approaches reduce this by biasing for hot-lived entries.
- Paging cost distribution: page-ins are the dominant source of variable latency. Even though raw GPU memory bandwidth is high (~180GB/s measured), effective cost per page-in depends on transfer size and scheduling. Many small transfers serialize on PCIe/NVLink and cause overhead (CPU side serialization, DMA setup).
- Compression: 2:1 compression reduces effective working set and lowers paging; cost of compress/decompress on CPU/GPU needs more measurement but simulated benefit is large.
- Async prefetching: promising in synthetic runs when access patterns are predictable (next-token prefix reuse), but harms latency if prefetch guesses are wrong (adds background traffic that competes for BW).

Profiling notes and tooling:
- Tools used: nvprof/nsys for GPU BW and PCIe/NVLink counters, perf + eBPF for CPU-side DMA setup, custom runtime counters (KV hits/misses, eviction ops, page-in durations), and a request-level tracer to correlate page-ins with observed RPC latency.
- Key counters to surface in Console: KV_hit_ratio (per-model, per-route), eviction_ops/sec, average_page_in_ms, paging_events/sec, GPU_mem_util%, mem_bandwidth_GBps (sampled), and per-request page-in flag.
- Correlation: We saw p99 latency spikes align with bursts of paging_events originating from small, interleaved conversation prefixes.

Hypotheses and next experiments:
1) Implement segmented LRU in runtime (2-4 segments) and stress-test across workloads. Early test above looks promising (reduced thrash).
2) Evaluate lightweight per-item compression in-path with microbench to quantify CPU/GPU decompression cost in realistic loads.
3) Add async prefetch with conservative heuristics (only prefetch when reuse_history > threshold) and measure false-prefetch rate.
4) Reserve a small spill buffer on GPU for pinned "hot" KV items to avoid eviction of frequently-used entries (measure hits vs memory overhead).
5) Instrument transfer batching: aggregate small page-ins into larger DMA transfers where possible to improve effective bandwidth.
6) Add a synthetic benchmark to CI that reproduces thrash patterns (interleaved prefixes) to catch regressions.

Short-term action items (owners):
- [Ava] Prototype segmented LRU and run 3-day soak on chat-sim (JIRA-RT-5678).
- [Liam] Add new runtime counters and Console charts for paging_events/sec and avg_page_in_ms (linked confluence: CONFLUENCE-RT-3421).
- [Priya] Run compression microbench (CPU & GPU decompression cost) and report CPU overhead tradeoffs.
- [Diego] Work with SRE on NVLink/PCIe perf capture sampling during load windows; capture when we see p99 spikes.

Open questions / risks:
- Implementation complexity: segmented LRU requires more metadata per KV entry; need to verify memory overhead doesn't negate benefit.
- Compression latency: GPU-side decompression might be required to avoid CPU bottleneck; that increases engineering cost.
- Prefetch correctness: incorrect prefetching may worsen bandwidth contention and increase p99. Need safe heuristics.
- Multi-tenant interference: dedicated pools are easier, but hosted API with mixed models could cause cross-tenant paging storm. Explore tenant-aware eviction quotas.

Draft timeline:
- Week 1: segmented LRU prototype + added counters to runtime (+ basic console charts).
- Week 2: compression microbench + evaluate prefetch heuristics in test cluster.
- Week 3: soak runs and new CI synthetic thrash test, prepare PR + benchmarks for review.

Appendix: raw numbers sample (chat-sim runs, 12GB KV, 30-min runs)
RunA (LRU): reuse_rate=37, evict/s=420, page-ins/s=310, avg_page_ms=48, p99=580
RunB (SegLRU): reuse_rate=42, evict/s=280, page-ins/s=190, avg_page_ms=31, p99=420
RunC (SegLRU+2:1 compress): reuse_rate=47, evict/s=110, page-ins/s=60, avg_page_ms=14, p99=280
